pr_title: PemReader should close InputStream after reading certificates / priva…
pr_body:
…te key

Motivation:

At the moment we not close the streams once we are done reading which could lead to ta fd leak if the user not explicit close these. We should just close these once we consumed the streams

Modifications:

- Always close the streams
- Add unit tests

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/10974
pr_comments: Closing this in favor of https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/10983

comments: Yes at the moment we expect you to call close... That said I can't think of a good reason why we shouldn't call close here one we consumed the stream. I will open a PR to change this

> Clarified javadocs in #10983

/lgtm  
and I found this bug by use dubbo , and I will report this bug to dubbo too, thanks~

review_comments: I think it's weird API to close things we didn't open. Open and close should be symmetric in the code.
I am a bit on the fence here as well... Maybe we should just add some docs to `SslContextBuilder` and explain that the user is responsible to close the input stream ?
Adding JavaDoc sounds much better. Because the `InputStream` is created and opened by the User so closure should be done by the User too.
